questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My crucial aspects were mainly interests in terms of my degree.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The visiting students office always made sure to send out information, thereby giving us a great and secure start to our exchange.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance by the visiting students office and the student association upon arrival. Many arrangements for settling in, getting to know my fellow exchange students, etc. were made for us. That helped immensely.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many options were available in terms of price range, where it was placed in the city, etc.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could either stay at a catered facility or a self-catered facility. I choose the last one, due to my personal needs and meal plans.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it can take some time finding a rhythm in terms of shared spaces, like the kitchen or the bathroom. Everyone has different needs and ways of living, and those has to be respected. Once you settle in, it really does become easy to live together in shared spaces.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of information, and some was quite ambiguous. The easiest way to find out was either calling the office or going there in person. They did host drop-in sessions for questions, which was extremely helpful. Once I figured out the process it was easy, but the doubts made it difficult to begin with.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process consisted of uploading personal information to your student record, and then waiting for that approval. Thereafter attending a drop-in session to get fully matriculated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help was available online, by emailing the visiting students office or attending their drop-in sessions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful due to a limited amount of courses available to visiting students, prerequisites and interests. However, the courses I did end up taking worked out for the better in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To either call the relevant office or go there in person to seek answers. They are busy, and by email it might take days to obtain an answer. So it makes the process much more smooth. Regarding courses, to accept that you might not be able to enroll in the ones you hoped for, but that it can turn out useful and exciting regardless.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The amount of knowledge I have obtained from the courses and the people teaching them has been overwhelming. It made me see things in new ways and learn about my own way of learning, building academic arguments and evolving my abilities, etc.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was high and they were well-organised. To be able to pass 60 credits (1 semester), one had to take three courses of 20 credits each. This is equivalent to 10 ECTS per course at UCPH, and in order to pass a semester there it has to be 30 ECTS. Just something to keep in mind, because the workload might be higher than at home (depending on the faculty and style of teaching of course).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite different from UCPH. It consisted of two parts: the lectures and then the tutorials. The lectures was around 50 minutes long and consisted of different teachers explaining and introducing themes, working methods, etc. on the subject of the course. The tutorials was also around 50 minutes, but the purpose was to explore said theme or method more in depth, creating discussions and developing the skill set for the specific course. Some tutorials also discussed the readings from the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took three courses:

- History of Art 1B - Art at the Crossroads of World Cultures, 500-1700 AD
- Ethnography: Theory and Practice
- Drawing and Design Thinking

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all of them for different reasons. 

The history of art course taught me about art from all over the world and how the discipline is in the midst of a decolonisation process. It made me realise some of our biases, our assumptions and how most of them can easily be put to shame. It made me able to further develop my ability to analyse and derive information and ideas of an art piece by the impact "close looking" have on it. 

The ethnography course taught me how much the studies of us as human in different scenarios makes our outlook on life change. How storytelling can affect the way we see different sets of people on a far greater scale than anticipated. Hereby also the possible problems with representation. 

The drawing and design course gave me a change to be creative in my studies, while still learning and seeing the way in which design and creating narratives help us change things in life, and how it is communicated to people. 

They all share a sense of realising a current bias in the way we view the world, and how it has changed and changes. They also share methods of analysis, problem solving and applying theory to practice in different ways.

questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general it is less expensive in the UK than in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many of the dates and schedules weren't listed on the websites, which made it difficult to figure out. My specific interest would end up becoming too expensive, so I dropped it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Various types of activities: social evenings, dances, badminton tournaments, hikes, museum trips, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the social ones the most, because it is a great opportunity to meet people, both visiting students and permanent students. Some are free, some are not. So that is also something to keep in mind.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh is a very walkable city, so it is a great city to explore on foot (even though their public transport is very efficient around the city center). It has many great parts of town, so it is fun to see the different sides of it. Otherwise to take a train ride into the countryside. Many of my friends have done it and absolutely loved it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy, because people here are very friendly and very warm. The only slightly difficult thing was keeping in mind that they ride and drive on the left side of the road.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is very likely that you'll end up having shared courses with local students. Since the tutorials are in smaller groups I met many local students that way and through group projects.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Probably getting accustomed to speaking in a foreign language (English) most of the time, both academically and in my life outside of university.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate the general sense of friendliness that the local culture consists of. The people are incredibly nice and talkative in a manner that makes one feel more at ease.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First of all to enjoy it fully, to keep an open mind and to accept the challenges because they will make you grow.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I've made and the people I have met during my stay has been one of the most rewarding experiences while on exchange. Apart from that how many challenges and unforeseen circumstances I can actually handle.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was settling in, getting used to the way courses are taught and finding a routine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Noone I can think of

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
